title: LA Lakers sell for a record $12.5 billion to ex-Disney CEO Iger and Jared Kushner’s brother Josh
facts: Former Disney CEO Bob Iger and venture capitalist Josh Kushner agreed to purchase the Los Angeles Lakers.
The Los Angeles Lakers were sold for a record-breaking purchase price of $12.5 billion.
Josh Kushner is the brother of Jared Kushner, son-in-law of Donald Trump.
The sale of the Los Angeles Lakers requires approval from the NBA’s Board of Governors.
Billionaire Mark Walter previously became majority owner of the Los Angeles Lakers less than a year prior.
The Los Angeles Lakers have won 17 NBA championships in franchise history.
The Los Angeles Lakers most recently won the NBA championship during the 2019-20 season.
Mark Walter's firm Guggenheim Investments owns the Los Angeles Dodgers baseball team.
Mark Walter's previous deal to buy a majority interest valued the Lakers at $10 billion.
Mark Walter had been running the Los Angeles Lakers since October.
The Wall Street Journal reported that an internal whistleblower complaint regarding Guggenheim Investments sparked a federal investigation.
The holding company Thrive Eternal is expected to participate in financing the purchase of the Lakers.
Josh Kushner is slated to become the controlling owner of the Los Angeles Lakers.
Bob Iger is expected to serve in a leadership capacity within the Los Angeles Lakers organization.
ESPN was the first media outlet to report the sale agreement for the Los Angeles Lakers.
